title: Refrigeration Cycles
description: Cold is not made, it is moved: a refrigerator pumps heat from the cold end to a warmer place, and the second law sets the least work that takes. At 4 K, rejecting to room temperature, each watt of cold costs at least seventy of work, and real machines need three times that. A gas cools as it expands only below its inversion temperature, so helium must first be cooled by expansion engines to near 10 K before a valve can liquefy it. Rejecting heat to Titan's 94 K air costs a third as much. Unlocks the Helium Liquefier.

puzzle.goal: A perfect refrigerator takes heat from T_c and rejects it at T_h. From Q_h/T_h = Q_c/T_c and W = Q_h − Q_c, write the heat removed per unit of work, COP.
puzzle.name: Carnot refrigerator
puzzle.ask: Find COP for a cold end at 4.2 K rejecting to Th = @{Th} K.
puzzle.method: No entropy is made: the heat leaving at T_h carries away exactly the entropy brought in at T_c.
